maria (eng-arch): Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about splitting large on-prem blobs into resumable slices for flaky transport and resuming apply without re-fetching full blob. Thoughts?

jamie (onprem): +1. operator UX needs resume to be reliable. question: how do we verify partial integrity? per-slice checksums?

sanjay (eng-runtime): Per-slice strong checksum + per-blob merkle root. And keep a small manifest mapping slice id -> checksum + sequence number.

taylor (ops): Also need activation fencing. if partial applied and we failover, we must not double-apply.

maria (eng-arch): Agreed. Proposal: manifest carries "apply-window" markers and "resume-token" that the operator stores. Operator run should be idempotent with window semantics.

kevin (eng-sre): How about a small state machine: DOWNLOADING -> VERIFYING -> STAGED -> ACTIVATING -> ACTIVATED. Resume allowed from VERIFYING or STAGED only.

jamie (onprem): Can we stream-verify while downloading to avoid extra IO? i.e., compute running merkle.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Yes, but for encrypted blobs we have to decrypt then hash. For chunked encryption we can handle chunk-level MACs.

maria (eng-arch): UX tradeoff: narrower slices => smaller retry cost, but more manifest entries. Larger slices => fewer seeks. We should default to ~8MB slices and expose config.

taylor (ops): Also need to consider operator bandwidth — we should support parallel slice fetch with a concurrency limit and backoff when retries spike.

deploy-bot: deploy 4951234570: config update pushed to test cluster for chunking defaults.

kevin (eng-sre): Failure modes: partial slice corrupt -> must mark slice as bad and retry from different peer. Peers might be proxies in air-gapped setups.

jamie (onprem): On air-gapped nodes, peers are operator-provided proxies. We need clear contract: proxy must not reorder slices and must support range fetch.

maria (eng-arch): Interface boundary: we define a small "slice transport API" for proxies: GET /bundle/:id/slice/:n -> returns slice bytes + checksum header. Also GET /bundle/:id/manifest.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Implementation detail: manifest signed by control-plane key. Proxies only relay bytes; verification happens on node.

taylor (ops): Ops ask: can we support resuming apply across upgrades? e.g., node reboots mid-apply and we resume after new agent version.

maria (eng-arch): We'll include agent-version compatibility in manifest. If agent can't resume, fallback is to re-fetch full blob and run apply in safe mode.

kevin (eng-sre): Observability: expose metrics: slices_total, slices_failed, resume_count, average_resume_latency.

jamie (onprem): Playbook note: operator should run `rictl resume <bundle>` to resume broken applies. CLI will surface which slices succeeded and which pending.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Security: avoid leaking artifact layout via proxies. Keep manifest minimal and make per-operator ACLs.

maria (eng-arch): Edge case: tombstone/garbage collection while resume token exists. We should have a retention TTL for partially-applied bundles. Operator must pin bundle until activation or explicit abort.

taylor (ops): That means garbage collector must consult resume-store. Add grpc endpoint for pin/unpin.

kevin (eng-sre): Rollback story? If activation fails, we keep previous version active and mark bundle as failed; allow operator to inspect diffs. No auto-rollback unless operator opts in.

jamie (onprem): Consider alternate: two-phase activation where we stage into a staging dir and swap symlink on success. simpler for rollback.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Two-phase swap needs atomic rename. On some filesystems rename across mounts is not atomic. Document constraints.

maria (eng-arch): Action items: 1) write RFC appendix with slice transport API + manifest schema 2) protototype merkle streaming verify 3) add resume-store retention TTL config 4) add CLI resume UX. Anyone want to own?

jamie (onprem): I'll take RFC appendix + CLI bits.

sanjay (eng-runtime): I'll prototype streaming verify.

kevin (eng-sre): I'll spec metrics and GC contract.

taylor (ops): I'll write operator playbook snippet.

maria (eng-arch): Great. We'll sync in next arch sync. Thanks.
